summary.name: Geometric Illustration. Category: Drawing and Illustration. The label was normalized from source descriptions, so it is not a verbatim source title.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: figures, objects and environments are built from a limited geometric vocabulary. Angles, proportions, line weights and palette are shared across the scene. Forms are decomposed, assembled and resized while identity and visual balance are preserved. Source review (medium confidence) shows triangles, rectangles and circles with a shared proportion language.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: Geometric Illustration is listed as a good fit for Punctuation Zoom and Radial Logo Burst, and is paired with shape-morph transitions and Swiss-grid typography. Inferred from those pairings: brand idents, logo stories, concept transitions and poster or design-system intros. Explainer or narrative suitability is unspecified.
summary.limitations: Punctuation Zoom needs an actual punctuation mark, and Radial Logo Burst needs an approved mark; neither should be invented. Gaze following needs eye layers or a rig. Blobby organic morphs, new colours mid-morph and continuous morphing without holds should be avoided. Source review covered only sampled seconds 1–8, with no verified audio or continuous motion.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent. The cream #F3EFE4 is only an illustrative swatch, not a required canvas, so choose the background from the scene. Suggested, not approved, tokens: foreground #253849 navy, accent_1 #BF6D45 terracotta, accent_2 #638878 sage. Navy-on-background contrast is 10.501 and passes body text. Terracotta and sage (3.33 and 3.433) are decorative only. Gradients are disabled. Task-provided exact colours override these suggestions, and source example hues are not constraints.
summary.motionAndInteraction: For video, all state derives from seekable composition time, with one owner per animated property, typically a paused GSAP timeline. Smooth authored movement suits assembly, while sharp cuts, impacts and reading holds stay deliberate. Optional references: motion-038 punctuation zoom and motion-039 radial burst (waves, confetti, circular palette inversion). Chapter and story scroll patterns (motion-012 and motion-015) apply only to interactive delivery. Gaze tracking (motion-006) is optional and needs eye layers.
summary.audio: Style-level audio is unspecified and no audio layer is mandatory. Options depend on topic and audience: restrained background music, voiceover, sound effects on assembly actions, ambience or silence. No genre, tempo, instrument or voice is assigned. Beat sync requires actual audio analysis, so motion-039 pulse timing is unverified against sound. Without supplied audio, state assumptions and do not default to instrumental music.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are mandated. Optional inputs: task-provided exact colours, approved punctuation or mark geometry for motion-038 and motion-039, and eye layers or a rig for motion-006. Fonts and geometry should load before animation construction. Motion-038 and motion-039 cite review evidence tied to the same style-cue hash. Absence of these assets is not a blocking question.
summary.combinations: Geometric Illustration is coherent alone. Suggested support: style-100 for shape-morph transitions, where figures decompose and morph along shared pivots, holding each assembled figure with shared angles and palette. Style-001 Swiss grid suits posters or design-system intros: flush-left sans type, primary tokens only, no Swiss red, no centered text, and shapes and text on one grid.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: SVG is the primary choice, with optional tldraw authoring, p5.js for parameterized modules, Paper.js for vector paths, or Delaunator for 2D triangle fields. Motion engine: GSAP paused timeline. Motion or Anime.js are optional, with one property owner each. Pipeline: HyperFrames by default, Remotion only with a recorded limitation. chroma.js validates palette contrast. Verify seeks, decoded frames and a contact sheet.
